items.narrative_markdown:
# Birthplace of Elizabeth Mariah (Turnbow) Barker (c. 1823)

**Conclusion (Probable):** Elizabeth, wife of the English-born blacksmith and farmer Jonathan Barker of Jasper and Smith counties, Mississippi, was born about 1823 in **Alabama**, not England. The FamilySearch tree records her as Elizabeth Mariah Turnbow (KWJ6-RPH). The "England" birthplace attached to her comes from an indexing error.

## The problem

The online index to the 1850 U.S. census for Jasper County, Mississippi, gives Elizabeth Barker's birthplace as England.[1] Later records give Alabama, and one daughter said Mississippi. Her birthplace decides where to look for her birth family.

## The evidence

**1850 — the original page.** On the handwritten 1850 schedule, the Barker household reads: Jonathan Barker, 30, blacksmith, born *England*; Elizabeth, 27, born *Alabama*; Sarah Martha, 4, born *Mississippi*; Amanda P., 2.[2] The informant is not named; in practice it was usually the wife or husband. This is an original record.

**Her own household, 1860-1880.** Every later census of the household gives Alabama for Elizabeth: 1860 Smith County (about age 36),[3] 1870 Smith County (about 47),[4] and 1880 Raleigh, Smith County (56, wife of "John" Barker, born England).[5] Each was taken by a different enumerator. All of these answers come from Elizabeth's own household, so they show one consistent family answer over thirty years.

**Her daughters.** In 1880, daughter Martha S. (Sarah Martha) Lovett lived next door to the Barkers. She gave her father's birthplace as England and her mother's as **Alabama**.[5] Daughter Amanda Ainsworth, in another part of Smith County, gave her mother's birthplace as **Mississippi** in 1880 and 1910.[6][8] In 1900 she gave Mississippi for both parents, although her father was English.[7]

**The Turnbow family (context).** The tree names her parents as Robert F. Turnbow and Sarah Canterberry, married in September 1816 in Madison County, Mississippi Territory, an area that became part of Alabama in 1817. No record found here states that they were Elizabeth's parents. This is context only and is not used to prove the birthplace.

## Resolving the conflict

*England* is not testimony at all. It exists only in the modern index, and on the original page it sits on Jonathan's line. The indexer moved the birthplace column down one row: Elizabeth received her husband's "England," Sarah Martha received Elizabeth's "Alabama," and Amanda received Sarah Martha's "Mississippi."[1][2]

*Mississippi* is a second-hand answer from one daughter, repeated across three censuses with the same informant. One of those entries is plainly wrong about her father. Amanda grew up in Mississippi among relatives settled there since about 1830, and the family's earlier home in Madison County had been part of the Mississippi Territory. A child reporting a parent's birthplace from family memory could easily give that answer.

*Alabama* comes from the original 1850 page and three later censuses of Elizabeth's own household. Her next-door daughter gave the same answer.

## Limits

The tier is **probable**, not proved. Only the 1850 entry has been examined in the original. The 1860-1880 Barker entries were read from indexes. No record names the informant, and no record gives a county of birth. A county could come from an obituary, a Bible record, the original LDS record-of-members register for the Mississippi Conference, or the original 1860-1880 census pages. This conclusion does not establish her parentage, which needs its own research question.

## Sources

1. "United States, Census, 1850," index, FamilySearch, Elizabeth Barker in household of Jonathan Barker, Jasper, Mississippi (ark:/61903/1:1:M4L8-3SY).
2. 1850 U.S. census, Jasper Co., Mississippi, population schedule, image 73 of 104, Jonathan Barker household; FamilySearch image ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-DC1S-623.
3. "United States, Census, 1860," FamilySearch, Elizabeth Barker in household of Jonathan Barker, Smith, Mississippi (ark:/61903/1:1:M6GV-MGR).
4. "United States, Census, 1870," FamilySearch, Elizabeth Barker, Smith, Mississippi (ark:/61903/1:1:MFSR-DYF).
5. "United States, Census, 1880," FamilySearch, Raleigh, Smith, Mississippi, sheet 295C-D, John and Elisabeth Barker and Major W. and Martha S. Lovett households (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9YB8-HDX).
6. 1880 U.S. census, Smith Co., Mississippi, Beat 2, ED 104, sheet 310C, Asbery Ainsworth household; FamilySearch image ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYB8-WKM.
7. "United States, Census, 1900," FamilySearch, Mandy P Ainsworth, Beat 2 Summerland, Smith, Mississippi (ark:/61903/1:1:M9FS-YK8).
8. "United States, Census, 1910," FamilySearch, Amanda P Ainsworth, Taylorsville, Smith, Mississippi (ark:/61903/1:1:MPDG-3ZJ).

The indexer moved the birthplace column down one row: Elizabeth received her husband's "England," Sarah Martha received Elizabeth's "Alabama," and Amanda received Sarah Martha's "Mississippi."[1][2]

*Mississippi* is a second-hand answer from one daughter, repeated across three censuses with the same informant. One of those entries is plainly wrong about her father. Amanda grew up in Mississippi among relatives settled there since about 1830, and the family's earlier home in Madison County had been part of the Mississippi Territory. A child reporting a parent's birthplace from family memory could easily give that answer.

*Alabama* comes from the original 1850 page and three later censuses of Elizabeth's own household. Her next-door daughter gave the same answer.

## Limits

The tier is **probable**, not proved. Only the 1850 entry has been examined in the original. The 1860-1880 Barker entries were read from indexes. No record names the informant, and no record gives a county of birth. A county could come from an obituary, a Bible record, the original LDS record-of-members register for the Mississippi Conference, or the original 1860-1880 census pages. This conclusion does not establish her parentage, which needs its own research question.

Context:
- The project concerns William Jacob Honeyman (Hunneman) of Hutton Rudby, Yorkshire (tree person I1, buried 27 Mar 1783), weaver.
- q_001: When and where was he baptised — Edinburgh 2 Dec 1716 or Hutton Rudby 5 Apr 1719?
- q_002: Where did his father William Hunneman (d. 1737 Hutton Rudby, tree person I2) originate — specifically, is a Scoonie, Fife record his origin?

Key tree persons:
- I1: William Jacob Honeyman (Male, d. 1783) — subject
- I2: William Honniman (Male, d. 1737) — father of I1
- I3: Phillis Mackannel (Female) — mother of I1
- I4: Catherine Billingham Codling (Female, d. 1783) — wife of I1
- I5–I12: children of I1 and I4

Assertions summary:
- a_001: Baptism 5 Apr 1719, Hutton Rudby — "William Hunnyman baptised" — record role: child (src_001, Hutton Rudby register)
- a_002: Relationship "Child of William" — record role: child (same record as a_001)
- a_003: Baptism 25 May 1717, Hutton Rudby — "Ralph Hunnyman, son of William, baptised" — record role: child (src_002)
- a_004: Baptism 1 Jan 1721, Hutton Rudby — "Eliz Honeyman, child of Wm, baptised" — record role: child (src_003)
- a_005: Christening 2 Dec 1716, Edinburgh — "William Honniman christened" — record role: child (src_004, Edinburgh register)
- a_006: Relationship "Child of William Honniman and Elizabeth Duncan" — record role: child (same record as a_005)
- a_007: Burial 27 Mar 1783, Rudby — "Willm Honeyman buried" — record role: deceased (src_005)
- a_008: Birth c. 1717 calculated from age 66 at burial — record role: deceased (src_005)
- a_009: Marriage 19 Jul 1738, Hutton Rudby — "William Huneman married Catherine Codling" — record role: groom (src_006)
- a_010: Burial 9 May 1738, Rudby — "Phyllis Hunneman buried" — record role: deceased (src_007)
- a_011: Residence 5 Jan 1724, Scoonie, Fife — "William Honeyman (wife Janet Blyth) resident at Scoonie, Fife, baptising a child" — record role: father (src_008)
- a_012: Burial 22 Aug 1737, Hutton Rudby — "William Hunneman buried" — record role: deceased (src_009)
- a_013: Burial 5 Apr 1783, Rudby — "Catherine, wife of Wm Honeyman, buried" — record role: deceased (src_010)
- a_014: Occupation "weaver" at burial 27 Mar 1783 — record role: deceased (src_005)
- a_015: Marriage 20 Aug 1738, Rudby (bishop's transcript) — "William Hunneman married Catharine Codling by banns" — record role: groom (src_006)

Important notes:
- a_001 and a_005 are COMPETING baptism assertions for the subject I1 — one is Hutton Rudby 1719, the other Edinburgh 1716. Both should be linked to I1 as competing evidence; do not rule either out at this stage.
- a_003 and a_004 are siblings of I1 (Ralph and Elizabeth) — these name their father as William, linking them to I2. Create stub persons for Ralph and Elizabeth if not already in the tree.
- a_006 names "Elizabeth Duncan" as mother in the Edinburgh record — this is a DIFFERENT mother from I3 (Phillis Mackannel), which is a key conflict for q_001/q_002. Do not merge — note this as a discrepancy.
- a_010 (Phyllis Hunneman burial 1738) links to I3 (Phillis Mackannel).
- a_011 (William Honeyman at Scoonie, Fife 1724, wife Janet Blyth) — this is a candidate for I2's origin but wife name does not match I3. Identity uncertain — treat as a candidate, not a confirmed link.
- a_012 (William Hunneman burial 1737) links to I2.
- a_013 (Catherine wife of Wm Honeyman buried 1783) links to I4.

Please review the existing plan for question q_001 ("Who were the parents of Patrick Flynn, b. ~1845, PA, d. 1908?") and revise or extend it to add plan items specifically covering unindexed FamilySearch digitized image volumes that should be browsed. 

Key project facts to keep in mind:
- Patrick Flynn, born ~1845 in Ireland, died 12 March 1908 in Schuylkill County, PA
- The 1850 and 1860 censuses place him in the household of Thomas Flynn in Schuylkill County
- Death certificate names Thomas Flynn as father (secondary informant: son-in-law James Brown)
- A will of Thomas Flynn (1881) is already in the sources (src_006, FamilySearch ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS4V-7TXW) — probate search (pli_006) is currently in_progress
- A deed from Thomas Flynn to Patrick Flynn (1881) is in the sources (src_008)
- A baptism record at St. Mary's Catholic Church, Pottsville is in the sources (src_005)
- The proof summary notes 1870, 1880, and 1900 censuses not yet searched; probate not yet complete
- The big timeline gap is 1860–1908

Focus specifically on what UNINDEXED image volumes on FamilySearch are worth browsing — things like:
1. Schuylkill County probate/orphans' court records (continuation/expansion of pli_006)
2. Catholic parish registers (St. Mary's Pottsville and neighboring parishes)
3. Schuylkill County deed books (for more land transfers naming Thomas or Patrick)
4. Naturalization/citizenship records
5. Any other record type with FamilySearch unindexed image coverage for Schuylkill County or Ireland of origin

Please use the research-plan and collections-search tools to identify concrete unindexed FamilySearch image groups for Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, covering the relevant date ranges, and add sequenced plan items to pl_002 (or create a supplemental plan). Report what you find and what you added.

openQuestions.question: Who was the father of Mikkel Nielsen Blyeberg (b. 20 Aug 1779, Stagstrup Sogn, Thisted Amt, Denmark)?

questionStatuses.nextStep: research-plan

quirks: Danish military levy rolls (laegdsruller) begin in 1789 and enroll every male from early childhood under his father's name — each son's entry sits directly beneath the father's, making the rolls DIRECT parentage evidence for a male subject.
Danish naming is patronymic before ~1850: 'Mikkel Nielsen' means Mikkel son of Niels, so the father's given name is Niels — the patronymic alone does not identify which Niels.
Vital events are recorded in parish church books (kirkeboeger); baptism entries name both parents. Civil registration is much later.
The Stagstrup parish register is only ~3% name-indexed on FamilySearch — plan to browse the register images by year rather than rely on the index.

Reading the current hypotheses and conflicts to understand the context for this new evidence.

Checking the log entries to cross-reference them before responding.

The log entries give me exactly what I need to evaluate this new record. Let me now check what assertions already exist from the Greenup County James Eastham household before forming a view.

This is enough context to respond meaningfully. Here is the reevaluation.

The death record changes the picture in one important way. Every note taken during earlier research speculated that the Robert Eastham who lived with the Burton household was probably the son of the older Robert Eastham — the one named as the father of the bride when Mary Ann Eastham married Ephriam Boggs in Greenup County in 1844. The death record removes that speculation: Robert's father was **James** Eastham, not Robert. That means the two Eastham men — the one who lived with the Burtons and the one who fathered the Boggs bride — came from different family branches, not the same one.

That has two meaningful effects on the active theories:

**The "two women" theory** (that Polly Burton and the Mary Ann Eastham in FamilySearch are different people) gets additional support. The Mary Ann Eastham who married Boggs had a father named Robert Eastham. Robert Jr. — who lived with the Burtons — had a father named James Eastham. Different fathers point to different Eastham families, making it harder, not easier, to connect the Boggs bride to the Burton household circle.

**The sibling theory** (that Robert Jr. and Polley Burton were brother and sister) stays open, and the death record actually gives it more structure. If that theory is right, Polley's parents would also be James and Elizabeth Eastham. Earlier research found a James Eastham and an Elizabeth Eastham listed in the same Greenup County household in the 1850 census — the county where Robert Jr. said he was born. That family is already in the project. Whether the James and Elizabeth from the 1850 census are Robert Jr.'s parents or his siblings (the birth years in a census are approximate and routinely off) is something the death record itself could help settle if the informant is known.

To formally bring this record into the project so the analysis can be updated, I need the source information — the FamilySearch link or record number, or if you found it in a microfilmed register rather than online, the film number and page. Do you have that? If not, I can search the Kentucky civil death registration records, which do cover Pulaski County for 1861, and try to locate it.

items.notes: Primary hypothesis for q_001. The Boggs/Eastham marriage record (src_005, a_115) provides direct evidence of a separate Mary Ann Eastham who married Ephriam Boggs on 30 January 1844 in Greenup County — a woman who cannot simultaneously be Jahue Burton's wife Polly in Pulaski County. The 'Father of the Bride' Robert Eastham named in that marriage record (a_117) must have been born approximately 1795-1805 to have a daughter old enough to marry in 1844, making him too old to be the Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County) who co-resided with the Burtons in 1850 and 1860. Four census records consistently name Jahue's wife as Mary A. or Polly Burton but never state an Eastham maiden name, providing negative evidence against the FamilySearch merger. The 1880 census image of the Burton household (log_021) documents Polley A.P. Burton's father as Virginia-born and her mother as Kentucky-born; these facts are recorded in the log entry but no formal assertions have yet been extracted from that image, so no assertion IDs for those parental birthplace facts are available here.

items.claim: Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County, Kentucky; co-resident in the Jahue B. Burton household in Pulaski County in both the 1850 and 1860 censuses; married Margaret Rucker in Boyd County, Kentucky, 25 January 1870) is a sibling of Polley A.P. Burton (Jahue B. Burton's wife), both being children of a Virginia-born Eastham father and a Kentucky-born mother. This accounts for both Polley's possible Eastham maiden name and Robert Jr.'s persistent co-residence with the Burton family.
items.notes: Supporting hypothesis that would explain Robert Eastham Jr.'s appearance in two consecutive Burton census households while bearing a different surname. Key supporting pattern: Robert's sworn 1870 marriage bond (a_157, a_159) reports his father born in Virginia and his mother born in Kentucky. The 1880 Burton household census image (log_021) records Polley A.P. Burton's father born in Virginia and her mother born in Kentucky — an exact match with Robert's sworn self-report. However, no formal assertions have yet been extracted from log_021 for Polley's parental birthplaces; those facts exist only in the log entry notes and cannot be cited by assertion ID here. Open conflict on Robert's mother's birthplace: a_144 (Robert's 1880 census image, log_030, unknown household respondent) lists his mother as born in Virginia, directly contradicting a_159 (Robert's sworn 1870 marriage bond) which gives Kentucky. The bond is analytically superior — sworn self-report on an original document — versus a census entry from an unknown respondent with secondary knowledge. This conflict has not yet been formally registered in the conflicts[] section and remains open. NOTE on a_159 informant_bias_notes: those notes contain an error stating the conflict is with 'Polley A.P. Burton's 1880 census which shows the mother born in Virginia.' In fact the Burton 1880 census image (log_021) shows Polley's mother born in KENTUCKY. The real conflict is between Robert's own 1880 census (a_144, Virginia) and Robert's own 1870 bond (a_159, Kentucky). This error in the existing assertion should be corrected in a future assertions-only update.

items.description: Robert Eastham Jr.'s mother's birthplace: Virginia (1880 census image, a_144) vs. Kentucky (1870 marriage bond self-report, a_159)
items.independence_analysis: The two assertions draw on distinct record events created by different informants at different times. a_144 is a 1880 census enumeration in which an unknown household member reported Robert's parents' birthplaces to an enumerator; a_159 is Robert's sworn self-declaration on a 1870 marriage bond in which he personally stated his mother was born in Kentucky. The records are independent — neither was copied from the other, and they were created a decade apart. Both ultimately rely on Robert's personal knowledge of his own family origins, but the quality of transmission differs: the census entry is oral statement filtered through an enumerator and recorder, while the bond is Robert's direct written declaration.
items.weighing_analysis: Under GPS evidence-weighing principles, a contemporary sworn self-report on a legal document carries greater weight than a retrospective census entry made by an unknown informant. a_159 (1870 marriage bond) is primary information: Robert personally swore the statement on a legal instrument and is the most proximate source for facts about his own parentage. a_144 (1880 census) is secondary information: the reporter is unknown, the enumeration is retrospective, and census entries for parents' birthplaces are routinely less reliable than sworn legal statements. The bond is also closer in time to the events it describes. Additionally, the a_159 value (Mother=Kentucky) aligns with Polley A.P. Burton's 1880 census parental birthplace record (Mother=Kentucky), corroborating the sibling hypothesis (h_002) that Robert Jr. and Polley Burton share a common Virginia-born father and Kentucky-born mother.
items.resolution_rationale: a_159 (Robert's sworn self-report on the 1870 marriage bond: Mother born Kentucky) is accepted over a_144 (1880 census by unknown informant: Mother born Virginia). Primary sworn self-report on a legal instrument outweighs secondary retrospective census entry by unknown informant.

Robert Eastham named as Father of the Bride. This records a distinct 'Mary Ann Eastham' who married Ephriam Boggs, not Jahue Burton. Timeline analysis: the Robert Eastham who lived with the Burtons was born ~1823-25, making him too young (~20 in 1844) to be the father of a marriageable bride in 1844. Therefore two Robert Easthams exist: an older one (b. ~1795-1805, father of Mary Ann who married Boggs) and a younger one (b. ~1823-25, who lived with the Burtons). The younger Robert is likely the son of the older — making Mary Ann Eastham (Boggs bride) a sister of the Burton-household Robert, and possibly an aunt or cousin of Polly Burton. The FamilySearch tree person LYYX-DS1 labeled 'Mary Ann Eastham' linked to Jahue Burton may represent this Boggs bride rather than Jahue's actual wife. Greenup County is adjacent to Boyd County in northeastern KY, where this Robert family later settled.

Transcribed Boyd County KY marriage bond image for Robert Eastham and Margaret Rucker, 25 January 1870 (Catlettsburg, Boyd County). CRITICAL SELF-REPORTED FACTS — Robert Eastham certified under oath: age 48 years (born ~1822); born in GREENUP COUNTY, KENTUCKY (not just 'Kentucky' as indexed); Father born in VIRGINIA; Mother born in KENTUCKY. Margaret Rucker certified: age 37 years (OR possibly 27 — handwritten digit uncertain; index gives birth year 1843 which implies age ~27, while 37 would imply birth ~1833; flagged discrepancy for image review); born in Greenup County, Kentucky; Father born Kentucky; Mother born Kentucky. Bondsman/surety: John P. Jones (signed as 'John. P. Jones' — NOT Jahue Burton). Ceremony to be held at house of D D Bell, Boyd County, KY. SIGNIFICANCE: Robert Eastham's self-reported parents (father=Virginia, mother=Kentucky) EXACTLY MATCH Polley A.P. Burton's parents' birthplaces from the 1880 census image (father=Virginia, mother=Kentucky per log_021). Robert's birthplace of Greenup County, KY connects him to the Eastham family center — the 1844 Boggs/Eastham marriage of Mary Ann Eastham (daughter of an older Robert Eastham) also occurred in Greenup County. This establishes that: (1) the Eastham family was rooted in Greenup County, KY with Virginia origins; (2) Robert Eastham Jr. (who lived with the Burtons in Pulaski County 1850-1860) was himself born in Greenup County; (3) the parental birthplace profile of Robert Jr. matches Polley Burton's profile exactly, supporting them as full siblings from the same Virginia-born father and Kentucky-born mother; (4) the 'older Robert Eastham' who was father of Mary Ann (Boggs bride, 1844) and father of Robert Jr. was himself likely Virginia-born and settled in Greenup County KY, consistent with the note in log_030 that the 1880 census enumerator recorded Robert's mother as Virginia-born (which may have been erroneous, per this self-reported bond saying mother=Kentucky)."
